verses.1: Rama, with a face parched by sorrow, spoke to all those who were seated before him with distressed minds.
verses.2: He asked them all to listen, wishing them well, and not to misunderstand, as he was about to reveal the kind of talk that existed among the citizens concerning his Sita.
verses.3: A very great and abhorrent scandal from both the citizens and the people of the country exists concerning me, and that talk cuts into my very vitals.
verses.4: He stated that he was born in the family of the great-souled Ikshvakus, and Sita too was born in the noble family of the great-souled Janakas.
verses.5: He reminded them, "O gentle one, you know how Sita was abducted by Ravana in the solitary Dandaka forest, and how I subsequently destroyed him."
verses.6: At that time, a thought arose in my mind concerning Janaka's daughter, Sita, wondering how I could bring this Sita, who had resided here, back to the city.
verses.7: Then, for the sake of proof, Sita entered the fire, and in your presence, O Lakshmana, the fire-god and the wind-god, who moves in the sky, declared Maithili to be sinless.
verses.8: Furthermore, the moon and the sun, in the presence of all the gods and sages, formerly declared Janaka's daughter to be sinless.
verses.9: Thus, she of pure conduct was entrusted into my hands by the great Indra himself on the island of Lanka, in the presence of gods and Gandharvas.
verses.10: And my inner self knows Sita to be pure and glorious, so thereafter, I brought Vaidehi to Ayodhya.
verses.11: This great accusation and sorrow, which is the very great slander of the citizens and the people of the country, exists in my heart.
verses.12: Any being whose infamy is spoken of in the world falls to lower realms as long as that word of disgrace is proclaimed.
verses.13: Infamy is condemned by the gods, while fame is honored in all worlds, and indeed, all great-souled individuals undertake their endeavors for the sake of renown.
verses.14: O best among men, I, being afraid of the fear of slander, would even abandon my life or you all, so what then of Janaka's daughter?
verses.15: Therefore, you should see me fallen into an ocean of sorrow, for I indeed do not see any existing sorrow greater than this.
verses.16: O Lakshmana, tomorrow morning, you must ascend the chariot driven by Sumantra, place Sita in it, and abandon her at the border of the kingdom.
verses.17: On the other bank of the Ganga, there is the divine-looking hermitage of the great sage Valmiki, situated on the banks of the Tamasa river.
verses.18: O Lakshmana, having abandoned her there in that solitary place, return quickly; may good fortune be yours, and carry out my command.
verses.19: And regarding Sita, you must not argue against this command in any way; therefore, O Lakshmana, go, for no deliberation is to be done in this matter.
verses.20: Indeed, great displeasure will befall me if you oppose this, for I have made you all swear by my arms and by my very life.
verses.21: Those who would speak to me with other words, attempting to persuade me in any way, are indeed always my enemies because they obstruct my desire.
verses.22: If you abide by my command, then respect me; let Sita be taken from here today, and obey my word.
verses.23: She had previously told me that she wished to see the hermitages on the bank of the Ganga, so let this desire of hers be fulfilled.
verses.24: Having spoken thus, Rama, the righteous one, with his face covered in tears, entered, surrounded by his brothers.
verses.25: With his heart engulfed by sorrow, he sighed like an elephant. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 45 ।। Thus ends the forty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
